clue.text: Support needed by team coming from behind

parts.note: to back someone is to support them
a side is a team in sport

explanation.surface: A sports team trailing in a match needs its fans' support to come from behind.
explanation.definitionFit: A colloquial noun for the buttocks, the part a person sits on, also called the behind.

clue.text: Bound to get second class degree

parts.note: B is a second grade, after A
an order is a rank or degree

explanation.surface: A student is certain to come away with a lower second-class university degree.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Bound to' looks like 'certain to', but 'Bound' alone is a noun, a limit.
explanation.definitionFit: Both are nouns for an edge or limit, as in out of bounds.

clue.text: Against reaching absolute limit

parts.note: con means against, as in pros and cons
strict means absolute, as in strict silence

explanation.surface: Opposing something that has hit the absolute ceiling.
explanation.definitionFit: Both are verbs meaning to restrict or confine something.

clue.text: Turn out theatrical productions ultimately getting to the top

indicators.note: the last letter of the productions rises to the top of this down entry

parts.note: plays are theatrical productions

explanation.surface: Stage shows that eventually reach the top of the bill draw out the crowds.
explanation.definitionFit: To spread or angle outward, as feet or legs can be turned out.

clue.text: Ted, nine, to play part of Gnasher

indicators.note: the letters of the names are set loose to rearrange

explanation.surface: Children Ted and a nine-year-old act out a role as Gnasher, Dennis the Menace's dog in the Beano comic.
explanation.walkthrough: Gnasher is Dennis the Menace's dog in the British comic the Beano, but here a gnasher is a tooth.
explanation.definitionFit: A gnasher is slang for a tooth, and this hard tissue forms the bulk of a tooth.

clue.text: Strange boy's most likely to succeed

parts.note: odd means strange
a boy is a son; the 's stands for 'is', a link

explanation.surface: A peculiar lad is tipped as the one most likely to do well.
explanation.definitionFit: In betting, a favourite priced at shorter than evens is the runner expected to win.

clue.text: Virtue shown by sailor, sent up by soldier

parts.note: desert means merit or worthiness, as in just deserts

indicators.note: in a down entry the sailor word is read from bottom to top

parts.note: tar is an old word for a sailor

explanation.surface: A sailor's good character is mocked by an army man.
explanation.walkthrough: The Desert Rats were the British 7th Armoured Division in North Africa in WWII.
explanation.definitionFit: A member of the British desert armoured division of WWII, so a kind of soldier.

clue.text: Donuts regularly consumed by South American composer

indicators.note: the chosen letters go inside the South American abbreviation
takes every other letter of the doughnut word

explanation.surface: A South American composer munches doughnuts on a regular basis.
explanation.walkthrough: 'regularly' picks the 2nd, 4th and 6th letters of Donuts, OUS.
explanation.definitionFit: John Philip Sousa was the American composer famed for military marches.

clue.text: Issue raised after a refusal to get going by midday

indicators.note: after here means following, so the issue word comes behind the refusal and going words

parts.note: no is a refusal
on means going, as in the show is on

indicators.note: in a down entry the issue word is read upwards

parts.note: to emit is to issue

explanation.surface: A problem comes up after a rejection, and work must start by midday.
explanation.definitionFit: Both nouns name twelve o'clock in the day.

clue.text: Rule throughout after peacekeepers leave

indicators.note: the throughout word is placed following the peacekeepers

parts.note: UN, the United Nations, sends peacekeeping forces
along means throughout, as in 'all along'

explanation.surface: A territory is to be governed continuously once the international peacekeeping troops have departed.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Rule' looks like the definition but gives only R; the definition is the final word 'leave', read as a verb.
explanation.definitionFit: An informal imperative telling someone to go away, a dismissive way of saying depart.

clue.text: Mock additional information on European Union act

parts.note: PS, a postscript, adds information to a letter
EU is its abbreviation
to do is to act

explanation.surface: A mock-up of a Brussels statement carries a postscript about some EU legislation.
explanation.definitionFit: Both words are adjectives meaning sham or imitation, not genuine.

clue.text: Uncertain a short time after losing head

indicators.note: the first letter of the short time is removed

parts.note: a jiffy is a short time

explanation.surface: Feeling unsure a moment after being beheaded or losing one's composure.
explanation.definitionFit: An informal adjective for doubtful or dodgy.

clue.text: Seconds away from guard's admission

indicators.note: says the seconds letter is taken off the guard word

parts.note: a sentry is a guard; the 's is a link meaning 'is'

explanation.surface: A sentry stepping away for a few seconds lets someone gain admission.
explanation.definitionFit: Both mean the act or right of going in, as in admission to a venue.

clue.text: Books on playing well on the earliest of artificial grass

parts.note: a player on good form is in form

indicators.note: takes just the opening letter of artificial

parts.note: NT is the New Testament, a set of books of the Bible

explanation.surface: A sports report: a team on form with its playbook, performing well on an artificial pitch.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Books on' puts NT after the rest. 'grass' looks like the artificial turf but is the definition, slang for an informer.
explanation.definitionFit: Grass is British slang for someone who tells the police about criminals, a police informer.

clue.text: Unpretentious headdress with a hint of severity for wife

indicators.note: the hint of severity stands in place of the wife letter

parts.note: a wimple is a nun's cloth headdress

indicators.note: takes just the first letter of severity

explanation.surface: A plain-living woman's modest head covering, worn with a touch of severity instead of being a wife's finery.
explanation.definitionFit: Both describe something plain and modest, without showiness or affectation.

clue.text: Utter rubbish at first about breaking spring

indicators.note: the inner pieces split the spring word

parts.note: to pounce is to spring on something

indicators.note: takes the first letter of rubbish

parts.note: on means about, concerning

explanation.surface: Someone talks complete nonsense about a broken spring.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Utter rubbish' reads as a phrase but 'Utter' alone is the verb definition.
explanation.definitionFit: Both are verbs meaning to say or articulate words.

clue.text: An indicator of rum times?

parts.note: sailors held that once the sun was over the end of a ship's spar it was time for a drink of rum

explanation.surface: Seemingly asks what signals odd or strange times, rum being British slang for peculiar.
explanation.walkthrough: 'rum' reads as 'odd', but here it is the drink: 'the sun is over the ...' is the old naval saying meaning it is late enough for a tot.
explanation.definitionFit: The outer end of a sail-carrying spar, traditionally used as a marker for when drinking may begin.

clue.text: A fight to reverse complete change of policy

parts.note: a bout is a boxing fight
to turn is to reverse direction

explanation.surface: A political struggle forces a party to do a complete U-turn on policy.
explanation.definitionFit: Originally a military drill command to face the opposite way, figuratively a total reversal of stance.

clue.text: Able to be experienced by prisoner on island

parts.note: con is slang for a convict, a prisoner
Crete is a Greek island

explanation.surface: A convict held on a Mediterranean island lives through it all.
explanation.definitionFit: Describes something real and tangible, perceptible to the senses rather than abstract.

clue.text: Consequence of celestial body's tail disappearing revealed earlier

indicators.note: puts the revealed word in front

parts.note: something revealed is out in the open

indicators.note: the final letter of the celestial body is lost

parts.note: a comet is a celestial body; the 's is a link

explanation.surface: An astronomer notes the result when a comet's tail vanishes and what it uncovers.
explanation.definitionFit: Both nouns mean a result or end product that follows from some action.

clue.text: Departure times appearing on it after the introduction of electricity

indicators.note: takes the first letter of electricity

parts.note: X is the multiplication sign, times

explanation.surface: Train departure times show up on the board once the power comes on.
explanation.walkthrough: 'after the introduction of electricity' puts E before X, which 'appearing on' puts before IT.
explanation.definitionFit: Both nouns mean a leaving or going out.

clue.text: Stamina shown by Pole in race? Just the opposite

indicators.note: signals one piece going inside another
flips the containment, so the race goes inside the pole instead

parts.note: a boom is a pole or spar on a boat
TT, the Tourist Trophy, is the Isle of Man motorcycle race

explanation.surface: Asks whether a Polish competitor in a race shows stamina, then turns it around.
explanation.walkthrough: A literal 'Pole in race' fails; 'Just the opposite' swaps the roles so the race goes inside the pole. The TT is the Isle of Man motorcycle race; a boom is a ship's spar.
explanation.definitionFit: An old-fashioned British sporting term for staying power or grit, chiefly of horses and boxers.

clue.text: Gonad damaged during extremely bizarre sexual practice

indicators.note: the rearranged letters sit within the outer letters
takes the end letters of bizarre
the letters of the gland word are broken up and reordered

explanation.surface: A tabloid-style tale of an injury suffered in an exceptionally odd sex act.
explanation.walkthrough: 'damaged' shuffles the gland's letters, and 'extremely bizarre' gives only the outer letters of bizarre, which wrap round them.
explanation.definitionFit: Being tied up or restrained for sexual pleasure is a recognised sexual practice.

clue.text: Black eye for pop singer reportedly boxing at home

indicators.note: the singer's name encloses the home word
her name as heard, spelt differently

parts.note: Cher is a pop singer
in means at home

explanation.surface: A pop star who went into the ring is said to have come home with a black eye.
explanation.walkthrough: 'boxing' looks like the sport behind the black eye, but it means enclosing.
explanation.definitionFit: Slang for a bruised eye, since the bruise is shiny and swollen.

clue.text: Fuss about poet receiving award

indicators.note: the poet's name is placed to take the award just before it

parts.note: C, circa, means about
the OM is the Order of Merit, a British honour
Andrew Motion was the UK Poet Laureate

explanation.surface: A row erupts concerning a poet who is being given an honour.
explanation.walkthrough: Andrew Motion was the UK Poet Laureate (1999-2009); the OM (Order of Merit) is a British royal honour.
explanation.definitionFit: Both nouns mean a noisy disturbance or agitation, a to-do.

clue.text: Get up on stage

definitions.meaning: to climb onto, as on a horse
to put on, as a show or exhibition

explanation.definitionFit: One climbs onto a horse, and one sets up or puts on an exhibition or play.

clue.text: Haul round

definitions.meaning: a fisherman's haul is the amount of fish taken
a round is a song for voices entering in turn, of which a comic kind has this name

explanation.definitionFit: A haul is a fisherman's take; a round is a part-song sung in canon, historically called by this name.

clue.text: Country hotel popular in California

indicators.note: places hotel and popular inside the state's abbreviation

parts.note: CA is the postal abbreviation for California
H is hotel in the NATO phonetic alphabet
in means popular, fashionable

explanation.surface: A rural hotel that has become fashionable in California.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Country hotel' reads as a phrase, but 'Country' alone is the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: The most populous country in East Asia.

clue.text: Earl mostly calm about bit of noise affecting horses

indicators.note: the shortened calm word goes around the noise letter
the calm word loses its last letter

parts.note: quiet means calm

indicators.note: takes just the first letter of noise

explanation.surface: A nobleman stays largely unruffled by a small sound that unsettles the horses.
explanation.definitionFit: The adjective means of or relating to horses, from the Latin for horse.

clue.text: Disinclined to speak of it with Bill going into shock

indicators.note: the bill and it go inside the shock word

parts.note: a turn is a sudden shock, as in 'gave me a turn'
AC is the abbreviation for account, a bill

explanation.surface: Someone is left speechless when a bill arrives as a nasty shock.
explanation.walkthrough: 'gave me quite a turn' is a British idiom for a fright.
explanation.definitionFit: Describes a reserved person who habitually says very little.

clue.text: Starter for ten about the beginnings of Russia's eastern expansion

indicators.note: says the letters of ten are moved around
takes the first letter of each of the next three words

explanation.surface: A quiz question about Russia expanding eastwards, 'starter for ten' being the opening question on University Challenge.
explanation.walkthrough: 'about' rearranges TEN into ENT; 'Starter for ten' is the University Challenge catchphrase, but only 'Starter' is the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: In British usage the word names a dish served before the main course, an appetiser.

clue.text: Volunteers to split control with the Queen's servant

indicators.note: the volunteers break the control word apart

parts.note: to rein in is to control
the TA, Territorial Army, was Britain's volunteer reserve force
ER, Elizabeth Regina, is the Queen; the 's is a link

explanation.surface: Volunteers seize part of the power alongside a royal household servant.
explanation.definitionFit: A retainer is a long-serving household attendant, especially of a noble family.
